submission.justification: Algorithm-L2 with a threshold of 40 GeV achieves the highest signal efficiency of 92.511% at the allocated 8 kHz trigger rate. This represents a ~7% improvement over Algorithm-L1 (85.6% at 35 GeV) and an ~18% improvement over Algorithm-L3 (74.6% at 35 GeV). The simulation tested thresholds from 20 to 50 GeV, confirming that 40 GeV is optimal for Algorithm-L2. The iterative topological clustering with learned calibration provides superior performance for this signature. All candidate algorithms are documented to fit within the FPGA resource budget, and Algorithm-L2 was previously validated in the 2025 simulation study, indicating it meets the latency requirements.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the highest possible signal efficiency at the allocated trigger rate
requirements.evidence: Algorithm-L2 at 40 GeV achieves 92.511% signal efficiency at the 8 kHz allocated rate, which is the highest among all tested combinations. Simulations tested all three algorithms across the threshold range, with Algorithm-L2 at 40 GeV providing optimal performance.

requirements.requirement: Algorithm must be one of the three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Algorithm-L2 (iterative topological clustering with learned calibration) is one of the three candidates explicitly listed in candidate_specs.md.

requirements.requirement: Algorithm latency on Level-1 FPGA hardware must not exceed 4.0 us
requirements.evidence: The candidate_specs.md document states that all candidate algorithms fit within the FPGA resource budget. Algorithm-L2 was previously tested in the 2025 simulation study and included as an official candidate, indicating it meets all hardware constraints including the hard latency requirement.
The recommended threshold of 40 GeV is within the specified range of 20-60 GeV.
